tasks.instruction: You've just heard about Astro from a friend who mentioned they use it to watch sports and local dramas. You decide to check it out for the first time. Look around this page. When you're ready, tell us: what do you understand about what Astro offers? Is there anything you'd want to do or look at next — and why?
tasks.response:
Okay first impression — the page is actually not bad. The pink is on brand, it's clean enough. 'Endless streaming with Astro One' — so it's a streaming platform. I get that immediately.

The recommended pack is Entertainment Zero at RM49.99. The name is a bit odd — 'Zero'? Zero what? Zero ads? Zero commitment? Zero content? The name doesn't tell me anything. I'd have to read to understand it's the no-contract option. That's a copy problem.

Visually I'm noticing the content thumbnails under the pack — I can see some titles but I can't really make them out clearly. I'd want to know — is there K-drama here? My WeTV has all the K-dramas I watch. If Astro doesn't have that then I'm not interested. The page doesn't tell me what content categories are included. That's missing.

The 'Three easy steps' section — that's actually quite nice, iconography is clean. Choose, Confirm, Stream. That I understand. But again, what am I choosing from? What content is on here that I can't get elsewhere?

If I'm being honest — this page is designed for parents, not for me. The WhatsApp support button, the FAQ section, the 'Still unsure?' copy — it's all uncertainty-management messaging. My parents would need that reassurance. I don't need to be convinced like that — I need to be excited.

Next action: I'd click 'Compare all packs' to see if there's anything targeted at my age group. Or honestly I'd check if any of my friends are posting about it on TikTok before I go further.

eval.confusion_signal: Entertainment Zero name is meaningless — 'Zero' communicates nothing about the product. Content categories not visible on homepage. Page tone reads as older demographic.
eval.trust_signal: neutral — page looks professional but doesn't signal relevance to this persona's content interests
eval.brand_comprehension: pass — understood it's a streaming platform
eval.value_proposition_clarity: missed — could not articulate why Astro is relevant to her specifically; no K-drama or creator-relevant content visible
eval.visual_hierarchy_effectiveness: off-target — hierarchy leads to pack pricing but persona needs content category visibility first
eval.information_gaps: What content is exclusive here vs WeTV/Netflix? Is there K-drama? Can I share clips from the content? Any social or creator features?

tasks.instruction: You're looking for a TV subscription for your household. You watch a mix of sports, movies, and local content. Browse through what's available here. Tell us what stands out, what's confusing, and what — if anything — would make you want to take action. If nothing appeals to you, explain what's missing or holding you back.
tasks.response:
Entertainment 12, Sports 12, Epic 24. What are these names? The number at the end — is that the number of months? Or number of channels? Or something else? I genuinely don't know what the 12 means in 'Entertainment 12'.

Entertainment 12 at RM39.99 — 'Best of content'. Okay. What content? It says 'Base | View more' but I shouldn't have to click through to understand what I'm paying for. On Netflix I know exactly what I'm getting. This feels like it's hiding the detail.

Sports 12 — RM69.99. I don't watch sports, so this is irrelevant to me. But I'm noticing — the sports categories listed are Sports, Sports Extra, Base. What's 'Base'? That appears in multiple packs. Is Base a shared foundation layer? That's confusing.

Epic 24 — RM159.99 for 24 months and I can see the Netflix, Disney+ logos on there. That's actually interesting because it bundles what I already use. But RM159.99 and a 24-month contract? I'm 22, I don't sign 24-month contracts. And I don't pay for things personally — I use family accounts or free tiers.

Nothing here speaks to me. The content is designed for households, not for a single young woman who wants K-drama and content creation fodder. There's no 'lite' or 'social' tier. There's no mention of what I can actually do with the content.

I'd leave this page and probably post a story asking if anyone uses Astro and if it's worth it. That's more useful to me than this page.

eval.confusion_signal: Pack name numbers (12, 24) unexplained. 'Base' tier label appears across multiple packs without clear explanation. Content detail hidden behind View more.
eval.abandon_trigger: No pack relevant to solo young female viewer. No lite or social tier. No content category signal for K-drama or creator-relevant content.
eval.trust_signal: neutral — Epic 24 bundle with Netflix/Disney+ created brief interest but contract length killed it
eval.pack_differentiation_clarity: blurry — could tell packs apart by price but the 12/24 naming and Base sub-tier created confusion
eval.personal_relevance: no — no pack matched her profile
eval.decision_friction: medium — rejected before deep friction, simply not relevant

session_summary: Syafiqah understood the product category but found no content signal relevant to her. Pack naming (Entertainment 12, Sports 12) is opaque — the number suffix was unexplained and the 'Base' sub-tier created confusion. No lite or young-skewed tier exists. She would exit and seek peer validation on TikTok rather than convert. Not a conversion target from current page design.
h1_verdict: falsified — pack differentiation was insufficient; persona could not identify a relevant pack to shortlist
